bsc_001: You can recognise it by standing right in the middle of the road across the square, a modest olive rather than a giant. It stands at the Largo do Mosteiro.
bsc_002: You can recognise it by its stiff, geometric, spiralling leaves and huge cones hanging from a 28 metre crown. It stands in the garden beside the Palace Hotel.
bsc_003: You can recognise it by its trunk, 7.15 metres round, the thickest on this page, with bark peeling off in long ribbons. It stands on the access road to the Palace Hotel.
bsc_006: You can recognise it by its storm-broken top, cut from 32.9 metres to 14 in a 2013 cyclone, its split trunk ringed by an iron railing. It stands at the Adro da Ermida de Sao Jose.
bsc_007: You can recognise it by standing beside the Via Sacra station marking Christ's first fall. It stands at the Passo da Primeira Queda.
bsc_008: You can recognise it as one of only two native species in the whole collection, its crown almost 21 metres wide, the widest native canopy here. It stands by the Capela de Sao Pedro.
bsc_009: You can recognise it by its thick, deeply fissured cork bark, visibly different from the conifers around it. It stands on the south slope above the Lago Grande.
bsc_010: You can recognise it by standing on the slope above the Fonte de Santa Teresa spring, on the Trilho da Agua water trail. It stands beside the fountain, at 45 metres tall.
bsc_011: You can recognise it by its trunk, 5.04 metres round, slightly narrower than the forest's other redwood. It stands about 70 metres from the Porta das Lapas.
bsc_014: You can recognise it by its height, 38 metres, a laurel relict from a forest type now found mostly on Atlantic islands. It stands by the Lago Grande, near the forest's cork oak.
bsc_015: You can recognise it by standing beside the bare surviving walls of the ruined Ermida do Sacramento. It stands about 30 metres from the Passo de Anas.
bsc_016: You can recognise it as the smaller of two protected cypresses within sixty metres of each other, standing directly over the shrine. It stands at the Passo de Anas.
bsc_019: You can recognise it by its trunk, 3.15 metres round, unusually thick for a species normally kept as a garden hedge. It stands at the entrance to the forest's tree nursery.
